task.description: Write test/specs/REQ-050.md and test code under test/letflow/engine/ (new test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs for the Expr module, plus updates to existing test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs for the gateway dispatch). Application-executable surface scope test: YES (real Elixir logic in expr.ex and transition.ex) -- full procedure applies, do not skip to Step 5. KNOWN FALLOUT TO FIX AS PART OF THIS STEP: test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs (~line 334) and test/letflow/engine/variable_merge_test.exs (~line 302) currently assert the OLD :gateway_not_yet_implemented stub error for :EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY -- REVIEWER (Step 2d) confirmed this is the correct, expected consequence of REQ-050 legitimately superseding that stub. Update both assertions to match the new real dispatch behavior (a zero-outgoing-edge or otherwise-non-matching gateway now returns {:error, {:no_matching_edge, node_id, evaluated_conditions}}, not the old stub tuple) as part of this step's own scope -- do not leave them red. REMINDER (per docs/anti-patterns.md's newest entry, added this session): keep every describe+test name pair comfortably under 200 characters combined -- ExUnit hard-fails compilation at 255 combined chars, and this project has hit that limit 3 times already this session. Put spec-citation/rationale text in a # comment above the test, not in the name string itself.
acceptance_criteria: a gateway whose second declared edge is the first to evaluate true routes the token down that edge, not the first or third -- an explicit ordering test, not a single-edge case

a gateway with a default edge declared FIRST and two non-default edges that both evaluate false routes the token down the default edge, proving the default is evaluated last regardless of declared position

a condition expression that raises a runtime error (undefined variable or type mismatch) is treated as false and evaluation continues to the next edge, rather than transitioning the instance to ERROR -- an explicit test distinguishing this from the no-match case
a gateway where no condition matches and no default edge exists transitions the instance to ERROR with a structured reason naming the gateway node_id AND the conditions that were evaluated
exactly one outgoing edge is followed in every passing case, asserted directly rather than inferred

a condition using an unsupported CEL feature (a macro, a type-conversion function, a collection function, or the ternary operator) evaluates to false via the catch-false rule rather than raising or erroring the instance, matching hasCelUnsupportedFeatures()'s boundary -- at least two such expressions tested explicitly

the CEL-to-expr translation is tested directly on each of its four documented rewrites (variables. prefix stripped, && -> and, || -> or, ! -> not with != passing through unchanged), rather than only end-to-end through gateway evaluation

the evaluator performs zero I/O and is deterministic, confirmed by inspection of its call graph and stated in the moduledoc, which cites src/engine/transition.zig's evaluateGatewayCondition() and src/expr/ as the ported reference and records which subset of the expression surface landed
the two pre-existing tests asserting the old stub error are updated to the new real-dispatch behavior, not left failing

result.summary: Wrote test/specs/REQ-050.md (rationale + AC traceability table) and a new test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs (30 tests covering translate_cel_to_expr/1's 4 rewrites individually, the unsupported-CEL-feature boundary with 5 distinct examples including a non-false-positive quoted '?' case, parse/1, eval/2's undefined-variable/type-mismatch/eq-neq-never-error shapes, evaluate_condition/2's catch-false composition, and purity/determinism checks). Updated test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs: extended the edge/3 fixture with an edge/4 opts variant (condition/is_default), and replaced the old :EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY stub describe block with 8 new tests covering declared-order first-match, default-declared-first-evaluated-last, undefined-variable and type-mismatch conditions falling through, macro-call and ternary-operator conditions falling through, the no-match/no-default structured error (naming node_id and every evaluated_condition), and the zero-outgoing-edge degenerate case -- each passing-case test also asserts exactly one token/edge followed via direct list equality (AC5). Updated test/letflow/engine/variable_merge_test.exs's AC5 composed-dispatch assertion from the old stub tuple to the new {:error, {:no_matching_edge, "gw", []}} result. Ran `mix test test/letflow/engine/expr_test.exs test/letflow/engine/transition_test.exs test/letflow/engine/variable_merge_test.exs` (0 failures, 72 tests + 1 property) and the full `mix test` suite (813 tests, 0 failures, 5 properties) to confirm nothing else regressed. All 9 acceptance criteria traced to at least one test case that would fail if violated (see test/specs/REQ-050.md's traceability table).
